description: Both chemical A and chemical B need to be added to a mixer for making bread. One unit of chemical A takes 30 seconds to be effective while one unit of chemical B takes 45 seconds to be effective. Because chemical A can be dangerous, there has to be at most a third as much chemical A as chemical B in the mixer. If there has to be at least 300 units of chemical A in the mixer and at least 1500 units of total chemicals in the mixer, how many units of each should be added to minimize the total time it takes for the mixed bread to be ready?

TimeChemicalA.definition: Time for one unit of chemical A to become effective

TimeChemicalB.definition: Time for one unit of chemical B to become effective

MaxRatioAtoB.definition: Maximum ratio of chemical A to chemical B

MinChemicalA.definition: Minimum units of chemical A required

MinTotalChemicals.definition: Minimum total units of chemicals in the mixer

objective.description: Minimize the total time required for the chemicals in the mixer to become effective (i.e., minimize the total time for the mixed bread to be ready).

constraints.description: Units of chemical A must be at least MinChemicalA
The total units of chemical A and chemical B must be at least MinTotalChemicals
Units of chemical A must be less than or equal to MaxRatioAtoB times the units of chemical B

ChemicalAUnits.definition: Number of units of chemical A added to the mixer

ChemicalBUnits.definition: Number of units of chemical B added to the mixer
